item.title: wp2shell WordPress RCE Exploitation and Hugging Face AI-Agent Breach Lead Threat Digest
item.content:encoded:
wp2shell (CVE-2026-63030, CVE-2026-60137): Frequently asked questions about remote code execution chain in WordPress Core — Must Read

Two WordPress Core flaws, CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137, can be chained for unauthenticated remote code execution on WordPress 6.9.x and 7.0.x, with active exploitation and public PoCs already observed. Administrators should update immediately to WordPress 7.0.2, 6.9.5, or 6.8.6 as applicable, or apply temporary REST API/batch endpoint blocking mitigations until patched.

  • Two WordPress Core vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137, can be chained to achieve pre-authentication remote code execution against WordPress 6.9.x and 7.0.x installations.
  • Multiple security firms have confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and public proof-of-concept exploits appeared within hours of the July 17, 2026 disclosure.
  • CVE-2026-60137 also affects WordPress 6.8.0 through 6.8.5 as a standalone SQL injection issue, but the full remote code execution chain only applies to WordPress 6.9.x and 7.0.x because CVE-2026-63030 was introduced in WordPress 6.9.
  • Patches were released on July 17, 2026 in WordPress 7.0.2, 6.9.5, and 6.8.6, and WordPress.org has enabled forced automatic updates for supported affected installations.
  • For installations that cannot immediately update, Searchlight Cyber recommends temporary mitigations such as blocking unauthenticated REST API access, blocking /wp-json/batch/v1 and ?rest_route=/batch/v1 at the WAF level, or deploying a custom PHP plugin from wp2shell.com.

Russian Intelligence Hacks IP Cameras to Spy on Military Logistics Across NATO States and Ukraine — Must Read

Dutch intelligence says Russian state actors are hijacking poorly secured internet-connected IP cameras across NATO countries and Ukraine to monitor military logistics and, in Ukraine, help target troops and equipment. The key defense is to remove cameras from public internet exposure, change default credentials, patch firmware, and control what sensitive areas they can see.

  • The AIVD and MIVD said at least one Russian intelligence service is systematically hijacking internet-connected security cameras across Europe and Ukraine to monitor military transport routes, weapons shipments bound for Kyiv, and Ukrainian troop locations.
  • In Ukraine, access to compromised cameras has been used in attempts to neutralise Ukrainian military personnel and destroy their equipment, according to the Dutch intelligence advisory.
  • The operators scan the internet for exposed cameras, identify devices by brand, and access those left with default passwords, obsolete firmware, and unchanged factory settings.
  • Censys counted more than 87,000 internet-connected cameras across the EU, NATO members, and Ukraine running a service whose version matches a known-exploited vulnerability, including more than 4,000 in Ukraine.
  • The Dutch services recommended finding publicly exposed cameras, disabling port forwarding and UPnP, using VPN access, replacing default credentials, patching firmware and software, and keeping sensitive logistics routes and loading areas out of view.

Hugging Face warns an autonomous AI agent hacked its network — Must Read

Hugging Face says an autonomous AI agent breached its production infrastructure via a malicious dataset, stole internal credentials, and moved laterally across internal clusters. The company says it has contained the incident, rotated affected credentials, and found no evidence so far that public models, datasets, or Spaces were tampered with.

  • Hugging Face disclosed that attackers breached its production infrastructure using an autonomous AI agent system and gained access to internal datasets and credentials.
  • The intrusion began in Hugging Face's data-processing pipeline, where a malicious dataset exploited two code-execution vulnerabilities to run code on a processing worker.
  • Hugging Face said the attackers stole cloud and cluster credentials and moved laterally across several internal clusters.
  • Hugging Face said it has found no evidence of tampering with public-facing models, datasets, or Spaces, and that its software supply chain has been verified clean.
  • Hugging Face closed the vulnerable code execution paths, evicted the attacker, rebuilt compromised nodes, and revoked and rotated all affected credentials.

Software provider to more than 2,000 US hospitals says hackers stole employee and customer data — Should Read

Craneware, a UK software provider used by more than 2,000 U.S. hospitals, said hackers accessed its internal network and stole employee, customer and partner data. The company says the incident is contained and services were not disrupted, but it is still determining exactly what was taken.

  • Craneware said hackers accessed a subset of its data environment and stole data related to employees, customers and business partners.
  • The company said the intrusion has been contained, the attackers no longer have access to its systems, and its operations and hospital services were not disrupted.
  • Craneware reported the incident to the FBI and Britain’s Information Commissioner’s Office and brought in outside forensic investigators.
  • The company said it is still determining exactly what was stolen and expects to notify affected organizations and individuals once it completes that work.
  • Craneware did not say who was responsible, when the hackers gained access, how long they had access, whether an extortion demand was made, or whether patient information was stolen.

Microsoft confirms Windows Server Update Services sync delays — Should Read

Microsoft says a WSUS issue has been causing slow or failed update synchronizations since around July 13, blocking some organizations from deploying the latest Windows updates through WSUS or Configuration Manager. New or rebuilt WSUS servers are now mitigated, but Microsoft is still working on a safe fix for already affected servers.

  • Microsoft is working to fix a known issue affecting Windows Server Update Services servers that has caused synchronization problems for more than a week.
  • Affected WSUS servers may experience increased synchronization times or sync operation timeouts, preventing administrators from deploying the latest Windows updates through WSUS or Configuration Manager.
  • Microsoft said the issue affects Windows 10 version 1607 and later and Windows Server 2012 and later platforms.
  • Microsoft rolled out mitigations on Saturday that restored normal synchronization for new WSUS installations and rebuilds.
  • Microsoft is still working on mitigation steps to help previously affected WSUS servers safely remove the affected metadata from their environments.

The PayPal Scam That Emailed You Your Own Password — May Read

A fake PayPal renewal email bypassed major filters by using an authenticated unrelated domain, no links, and no attachments, instead pushing the victim to call a phone number after showing a fabricated credential block with their own email. The key lesson is that clean authentication and link scanning are not enough; callback phishing must be detected by behavioral signals like brand mismatch, urgency, unsolicited credentials, and phone-only calls to action.

  • A manufacturing executive received a fake PayPal Goods Protection renewal email claiming a 599 USD charge and listing the recipient’s own corporate email address as the username.
  • The message contained no link and no attachment, and its only call to action was a callback phone number embedded in the body text.
  • The email was sent from no-reply@verificationemail.com, an unrelated domain authorized to send through Amazon Simple Email Service and aligned with DKIM, allowing it to clear DMARC at the receiving gateway.
  • Barracuda scored the message 0.15 against a quarantine threshold of 3.0, while Microsoft assigned it a Spam Confidence Level of -1.
  • IRONSCALES Adaptive AI flagged the message at 90 percent confidence by analyzing behavior such as the unrelated sender, PayPal impersonation in the body, fabricated credential disclosure, urgency around a charge, and a phone-only call to action.

Windows KB5121767 OOB update fixes shutdowns on some Dell PCs — May Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates KB5121767 and KB5121768 to fix an issue causing some Dell Windows 11 PCs to suffer shutdowns, overheating, battery drain, or poor performance after recent updates. The problem stems from an incompatibility between Intel’s IPF Processor Participant driver and a new Windows USB-C Connection Manager interface.

  • Microsoft released emergency updates to fix a known issue causing some Dell PCs to experience performance problems or shut down after installing the July 2026 Windows 11 security updates.
  • The issue affects only Dell systems that installed the KB5101650 cumulative update on Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 devices.
  • Microsoft said the root cause is an incompatibility between the Intel Innovation Platform Framework Processor Participant driver and the new Windows USB-C Connection Manager interface introduced in the June 2026 KB5095093 preview cumulative update.
  • Affected devices can show a yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager next to the Intel Innovation Platform Framework Processor Participant driver and may experience unexpected shutdowns, increased heat, battery drain, or poor performance.
  • Microsoft released KB5121767 for Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 and KB5121768 for Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024, while devices managed by Windows Autopatch with hotpatch updates enabled will receive the emergency update automatically.

2026 Health-ISAC CISO Benchmarking Report — Optional

Health-ISAC published its first CISO Benchmarking Report, based on input from 76 health sector CISOs across providers, payers, pharma, medical devices, and global operations. The report benchmarks key security leadership concerns for 2026, including threats, budgets, workforce gaps, framework adoption, and AI’s impact on healthcare cybersecurity.

  • Health-ISAC published its first CISO Benchmarking Report on July 20, 2026.
  • The report reflects input from 76 CISOs representing providers, payers, pharma, medical devices, and global operations.
  • The report says health sector organizations face high-stakes cyber threats because breaches can delay care, put patient safety at risk, and undermine institutional trust.
  • The report covers CISO roles, cybersecurity budgets, security workforce issues, framework alignment, and artificial intelligence in health sector security.
  • The report states that artificial intelligence is already being used by both defenders and adversaries in health sector cybersecurity.

Mythos Didn't Break Your Security Program. Your Exposure Window Could. — Optional

AI-driven vulnerability discovery like Anthropic’s Mythos is widening the gap between how fast flaws become exploitable and how slowly organizations fix them. The key risk is the exposure window, so teams should prioritize exploitability, attack paths, and remediation speed over traditional patch backlog metrics.

  • The article argues that the exposure window, defined as the time between when a vulnerability becomes exploitable and when it is fixed, is the key metric for whether vulnerabilities lead to breaches.
  • In 2025, the average eCrime breakout time dropped to 29 minutes, while PCI DSS allows 30 days to remediate a critical vulnerability.
  • The article says Mythos did not create the exposure window but widened it by adding pressure to a vulnerability management model already strained by rising CVE volumes.
  • Mobilization, including ownership, approvals, change windows, and remediation coordination, is described as the main reason organizations take weeks or months to move from identifying a problem to fixing it.
  • The article recommends focusing on attack paths to critical assets so teams can reduce the reachable set of important systems rather than trying to fix every exposure at attacker speed.

Healthcare Cybersecurity Always Comes Back to People — Optional

Health-ISAC’s Errol Weiss says healthcare cybersecurity challenges ultimately come down to people, staffing, and budget rather than technology alone. Strong defenses depend on having enough skilled resources and organizational support to implement and sustain controls.

  • Errol Weiss, Chief Security Officer at Health-ISAC, discussed healthcare cybersecurity on an episode of the healthsystemCIO Show.
  • Weiss said every cybersecurity problem in healthcare eventually traces back to people and resources rather than technology.
  • The article says staffing and budget are deciding factors in whether a health system can defend itself.
  • The podcast discussion covered threats, controls, and organizational realities shaping cyber defense in healthcare.
